name: Use cases, proposals, intents and proofs
description: Restructure Lastro around four entities: use cases (the application, with their regression proofs), proposals (every change, starting from prose), intents (reviewed natural-language changes to one use case each) and proofs (derived from approved intents, attached to their use case once they pass).

intents.name: One file per use case
intents.description: Each use case lives in .lastro/usecases/<id>-<slug>.json with id, slug, name, description, its proofs and the history of proposals that changed it.
intents.quote: `.lastro/usecases/<id>-<slug>.json`

intents.name: One file per proposal
intents.description: Each proposal lives in .lastro/proposals/<id>-<slug>.json with its prose, intents, review, proofs and status.
intents.quote: `.lastro/proposals/<id>-<slug>.json`

intents.name: Ids that are never reused
intents.description: Use cases are numbered UC-001... and proposals P-001... with the next free number, never reused; intents and proofs are numbered inside their proposal (P-007.I-03, P-007.PF-05) and keep that id forever.
intents.quote: A number is never reused, even after a use case is removed.

intents.name: Stable slugs
intents.description: Slugs are kebab-case and never change; a rename changes only the name.
intents.quote:
A
  rename changes `name`, never the slug or the id.

intents.name: Retire intents.json, spec.json and proof.json
intents.description: The workspace no longer writes intents.json, spec.json and proof.json; their content lives in the proposal.
intents.quote: `intents.json`, `spec.json` and `proof.json` go away

intents.name: propose creates a proposal
intents.description: propose(prose, { submittedBy }) creates the next proposal file and extracts its intents against the current use cases, with status open.
intents.quote: `propose(prose, { submittedBy })` creates `P-<n>` in `.lastro/proposals/`

intents.name: An intent changes one use case
intents.description: Each intent has id, slug, name and a natural-language description of the addition, removal or change of exactly one use case, and its provability (formal, empirical or beyond-proof with a reason); the old kind (behavior, invariant, preserve, non-functional) goes away.
intents.quote:
Each intent changes
exactly one use case

intents.name: Resulting use cases
intents.description: Extraction returns, for each touched use case, the combined after description; the SDK copies before from the use case, never the LLM.
intents.quote: before?: string;             // modify/remove: copied from the use case by the SDK, never by the LLM

intents.name: Intents list the proofs they replace
intents.description: Extraction receives every touched use case with its proofs and lists on each intent the existing proofs its new behavior contradicts, with a reason.
intents.quote: lists, on each intent, the proofs the new behavior contradicts and why (`replaces`)

intents.name: A removal replaces every proof
intents.description: For a remove, the SDK fills replaces with every proof of the use case without asking the LLM.
intents.quote: For a `remove`, the SDK fills `replaces` with every proof of the use case

intents.name: Bind the baseline
intents.description: The proposal records the baseline, a sha256 over the canonical use cases without their proofs, and who submitted the prose.
intents.quote: baseline: string;            // sha256 over the canonical use cases (without proofs) the prose was read against

intents.name: Check use-case references
intents.description: Extraction is rejected when a modify or remove names an unknown use case, an add does not reserve a new id and kebab-case slug, an add or modify has no after, or a touched use case does not have exactly one change listing at least one intent.
intents.quote: A `modify` or `remove` names an existing use case; an `add` reserves a new id and a new kebab-case slug.

intents.name: Check replaced proofs
intents.description: Extraction is rejected when an intent replaces a proof that does not exist or belongs to another use case.
intents.quote: The SDK checks that every replaced proof exists and belongs to the intent's use case

intents.name: Conflicting changes become decisions
intents.description: Change kinds that do not fit together on one use case, and intents that contradict each other on one use case, come back as decisions.
intents.quote: two intents that contradict each other on one use case come back as a decision

intents.name: Rewrite after on reject or amend
intents.description: Rejecting or amending an intent marks its use case's after stale; the reviewer writes the new after by hand or has the LLM recombine it from the remaining intents through the extract step, and that use case's intents need review again.
intents.quote:
The reviewer either writes the new `after`
   by hand or has the LLM recombine it

intents.name: Show what an intent replaces
intents.description: Review shows each intent with the proofs it replaces, their statements and reasons; approving the intent accepts the replacement and a reviewer who disagrees amends the list.
intents.quote: Approving the intent accepts the replacement.

intents.name: Review threads
intents.description: Reviewers comment on an intent, a proof or the prose, starting a thread resolved by the commenter or the submitter.
intents.quote: A comment on one intent, one proof or the prose, starting a thread.

intents.name: Open threads block approval
intents.description: Open threads, like unresolved intents and unanswered decisions, block approval.
intents.quote: Open threads, unresolved intents and unanswered decisions block approval.

intents.name: Proposal status
intents.description: A proposal moves through open, changes-requested, approved, proving, proved, applied and closed.
intents.quote: "open" | "changes-requested" | "approved" | "proving" | "proved" | "applied" | "closed"

intents.name: Review policy in config.json
intents.description: The review policy is read from the review block of .lastro/config.json (approvals default 1, submitterCanApprove default true); the legacy requiredApprovals key is still read.
intents.quote: `approvals` defaults to 1 and `submitterCanApprove` to true.

intents.name: The submitter is a reviewer
intents.description: The LLM is the author of the intents and the submitter is a reviewer whose approvals count unless submitterCanApprove is false.
intents.quote: A repository that wants a second pair of eyes sets `submitterCanApprove: false`.

intents.name: Record the policy reviewed under
intents.description: A proposal records the policy it was reviewed under, so a later config change never flips its approval.
intents.quote:
A proposal records the policy it
was reviewed under

intents.name: Approve when everything is resolved
intents.description: A proposal is approved when every intent is approved, amended or rejected and every decision and thread is resolved.
intents.quote:
The proposal is approved when every intent is approved, amended or rejected, and every decision and
   thread is resolved

intents.name: Stale approval on a changed baseline
intents.description: The approval hash binds the baseline; if the use cases changed since extraction, the approval is stale and the prose must be extracted again.
intents.quote:
if the use
   cases changed since extraction, the approval is stale and the prose must be extracted again.

intents.name: Carry review by change
intents.description: Re-extraction carries a review by change, use case and description, ignoring case and spacing; intents that changed lose their approvals.
intents.quote: Intents that changed lose their approvals (stale review dismissed); untouched intents keep them.

intents.name: Derive proofs from approved intents
intents.description: derive(proposal) writes pending proofs, each a clause or a scenario tied to one approved or amended intent and its use case, naming its model and subject.
intents.quote: `derive(proposal)` writes pending proofs for the approved and amended intents only

intents.name: A proof for every removal
intents.description: Every remove intent gets a proof that the old behavior no longer happens, or a decision when the model cannot express it.
intents.quote: A `remove` intent always gets a proof that the old behavior no longer happens

intents.name: No proof retired without review
intents.description: Derivation never retires a proof: supersedes is the union of replaces over approved and amended intents, and a broken proof that no approved intent replaces comes back as a decision sending the intent back to review.
intents.quote: derivation never adds to it

intents.name: New proofs name what they replace
intents.description: Each new proof that takes the place of a replaced proof lists it, so the old guarantee can be shown next to the new one.
intents.quote: Each new proof that takes the place of a replaced proof says so

intents.name: Run every use case's proofs
intents.description: prove(proposal) runs the proposal's proofs and the proofs of every use case except the superseded ones; a failing use-case proof is a regression.
intents.quote:
runs the proposal's proofs and the proofs of every use case (except the superseded
   ones)

intents.name: Regression run on its own
intents.description: lastro regress runs every use case's proofs alone.
intents.quote: run every use case's proofs alone

intents.name: Use cases without proofs
intents.description: A use case with no proofs yet is reported as unproved rather than failing.
intents.quote:
Until a use case has proofs, verification reports
it as unproved rather than failing

intents.name: Replaced proof that still passes
intents.description: A superseded proof that still passes against the new code is noted in the receipt, since the behavior may not have changed.
intents.quote: A superseded proof that still passes against the new code is noted in the receipt

intents.name: Apply only when every proof passes
intents.description: apply(proposal) refuses unless the proposal is approved and every proof, new and regression, passes.
intents.quote: `apply(proposal)` runs only when every proof passes.

intents.name: Proofs join their use cases
intents.description: apply moves each proof to its use case as a regression test, removes superseded proofs and appends the proposal id to history.
intents.quote:
moves each proof to its use case
   as a regression test, removes the superseded proofs, appends the proposal id to `history`

intents.name: Sync the use cases
intents.description: apply writes each resulting use case: adds the file, replaces description and name, or deletes the file of a removed use case, and records the new baseline in the receipt.
intents.quote:
It writes each `UseCaseChange` (adds the file,
   replaces the description and name, or deletes the file of a removed use case)

intents.name: Use-case diff in the receipt
intents.description: The receipt shows each use case added, modified (before and after) or removed with its intents, each replaced proof next to the proofs that take its place, each regression, and each replaced proof that still passes.
intents.quote: The receipt gains the use-case diff

intents.name: CLI around proposals
intents.description: The CLIs offer propose, status, review (approve, amend, reject, answer, comment, resolve), derive, prove, feedback, apply and regress, each taking a proposal.
intents.quote: lastro propose <prose-file> [--section <heading>] [--as <submitter>]

intents.name: Shared entity files
intents.description: The TypeScript, .NET and Go CLIs read and write the same usecases/ and proposals/ files.
intents.quote: Everything the framework generates or keeps lives in `.lastro/`

intents.name: The gate reads the proposal
intents.description: The plugin's gate allows source edits only while the current proposal is approved, its proofs are derived and its last run has not passed, and tells the agent to write prose and run lastro propose otherwise.
intents.quote:
The agent plugin
(`plugins/lastro`) and the live board (`plugins/lastro-board`) follow

intents.name: The review skill works on proposals
intents.description: The propose skill writes the prose as a proposal, runs lastro propose, asks the user each decision and each intent with the proofs it replaces, and runs lastro derive once the proposal is approved.
intents.quote:
an agent's plan is saved as the
prose of a new proposal

intents.name: The stop hook proves the proposal
intents.description: The stop hook proves the current proposal with the regression run and hands failures and regressions back to the agent.
intents.quote:
the stop hook and
both boards read the current proposal and the use cases instead of those files

intents.name: The board shows the proposal
intents.description: The progress board shows the current proposal's stages, its proofs, the proofs its intents replace and any regressions.
intents.quote:
the stop hook and
both boards read the current proposal and the use cases instead of those files

intents.name: The live board reads the proposal
intents.description: The live board reads the current proposal and the use cases instead of intents.json, spec.json and proof.json.
intents.quote: both boards read the current proposal and the use cases

intents.name: A plan becomes a proposal's prose
intents.description: An agent's approved plan is saved as the prose of a new proposal (.lastro/proposals/<id>-<slug>.md) and the agent is told to run lastro propose on it.
intents.quote:
an agent's plan is saved as the
prose of a new proposal

intents.name: All three SDKs
intents.description: The TypeScript, .NET and Go SDKs implement the four entities and the flow with matching hashes, checked by the cross-check tests.
intents.quote: A semantic change in all three SDKs (TypeScript, .NET, Go)

intents.name: The sandbox shows a proposal
intents.description: The sandbox shows the example as a proposal: intents grouped by use case with a before and after diff, proofs and regressions.
intents.quote: the sandbox example updated to the new format

useCases.name: Store use cases and proposals
useCases.after: The workspace keeps one file per entity: each use case in .lastro/usecases/<id>-<slug>.json (id, slug, name, description, proofs, history) and each proposal in .lastro/proposals/<id>-<slug>.json, with its receipt next to it. Use cases are numbered UC-001, UC-002... and proposals P-001, P-002... with the next free number, never reused even after a removal; intents and proofs are numbered inside their proposal (P-007.I-03, P-007.PF-05) and keep that id when a proof moves to its use case. Slugs are kebab-case and stable: a rename changes only the name. intents.json, spec.json and proof.json are no longer written.

useCases.name: Extract intents from prose
useCases.after: propose(prose, { submittedBy }) creates the next proposal file in .lastro/proposals/ with status open and sends the prose and the current use cases to an LLM through an AskJson transport with a fixed system prompt and JSON Schema (step "extract"). The answer lists intents, each the addition, removal or change of exactly one use case: id (P-n.I-nn), slug, name, a natural-language description of the change, change (add, modify or remove), the use case (an existing id, or a newly reserved id and slug for an add), a provability (formal, empirical, beyond-proof), a beyondProofReason ("none" or one of the five reasons) and a verbatim quote, and replaces: the existing proofs of that use case the new behavior contradicts, each with a reason (extraction receives every touched use case with its proofs in readable notation; for a remove the SDK lists every proof of the use case itself); one resulting use case per touched use case with its name and, for add and modify, the complete new description (after), all its intents combined, and the intents that produce it; decisions that reference intents by zero-based index; and notPromised items. The SDK fills each modify and remove with the use case's current description (before); the LLM never supplies it. The proposal (lastro: proposal/v1) records the baseline (sha256 over the canonical use cases without their proofs), the submitter, every intent proposed with no approvals, decisions D1, D2... with origin extraction, and the review policy. Intents have no kind. Without an LLM transport or a custom extractor, propose() throws.

useCases.name: Anchor every intent to the prose
useCases.after: Each intent stores its quote with start and end offsets into the prose (the intent map). The quote is searched verbatim first, then ignoring case and runs of whitespace from a word boundary. The whole extraction is rejected with an ArtifactError listing every problem if any quote is not found; a beyond-proof intent has no reason or a reason is unknown; a decision has fewer than two options, a recommended index out of range or an unknown intent; a modify or remove names a use case that does not exist; an add does not reserve a new id and a new kebab-case slug; an add or modify has no after; a touched use case does not have exactly one resulting use case listing at least one intent; or an intent replaces a proof that does not exist or belongs to another use case.

useCases.name: Turn ambiguity into decision cards
useCases.after: The extraction prompt tells the model not to guess when the prose is ambiguous and to return a decision instead: one question, two to four options each with a consequence, and the index of the recommended option, preferably about cases the author has not considered. Each becomes a decision card tied to the intents it concerns. Intents on one use case whose change kinds do not fit together (an add or a remove mixed with a modify, or a remove combined with anything) and two intents that contradict each other on one use case also come back as decisions. A card with origin extraction records the chosen option when answered and creates no intent.

useCases.name: Review intents
useCases.after: review(proposal, reviewer) returns a chainable review on a copy of the proposal (an approved proposal is reopened first). approve(ids) marks intents approved (an amended intent stays amended) and adds the reviewer to approvals once; approveAll() approves every intent that is not rejected; reject(id, note) sets status rejected, records the note with the reviewer's name and clears approvals; amend(id, description, patch?, note?) keeps the first original description, rewrites the description (optionally provability or beyond-proof reason), sets status amended and resets approvals to the amender alone. Review shows each intent with the proofs it replaces, their formal statements and the reasons; approving the intent accepts that those proofs will be replaced by proofs of the new behavior, and a reviewer who disagrees with the list amends the intent. A rejected intent drops out of its use case, replaces nothing and never reaches derivation or implementation. Rejecting or amending an intent marks its use case's after stale: the reviewer either writes the new after by hand (rewriteAfter(useCase, text)) or has the LLM recombine it from the remaining intents (recombine(useCase, instructions?), part of the extract step, through the same LLM or handoff), and that use case's intents need review again. done() returns the new proposal; unknown ids throw.

useCases.name: Comment on intents and proofs
useCases.after: During review, comment(target, text) starts a thread on one intent, one proof or the prose, recorded with the reviewer's name, and reply adds to it. A thread is resolved by its commenter or by the submitter. Threads live in the proposal file, so they work the same from the library, the CLIs (lastro review <proposal> --as <name> comment <id> "..." and resolve), an agent or a UI. Open threads are listed by pending() and, like unresolved intents and unanswered decisions, block approval.

useCases.name: Track a proposal's status
useCases.after: A proposal has one status: open while its review is pending; changes-requested while a reviewer has an open thread; approved once approval succeeds; proving once its proofs are derived; proved when every proof, new and regression, passes; applied once apply has synced the use cases; closed when it is abandoned. status lists the proposals with their status, and status <proposal> its pending items.

useCases.name: Enforce the team's approval policy
useCases.after: The review policy is read from the review block of .lastro/config.json: approvals, how many distinct reviewers must approve each intent (default 1, never less than 1), and submitterCanApprove (default true); the legacy requiredApprovals key is still read as approvals, and createLastro takes the same policy. The LLM that extracted the intents is their author and every person is a reviewer, the submitter included; with submitterCanApprove false the submitter's approvals do not count. An approved or amended intent counts its distinct counting approvers; proposed and rejected intents count zero. pending() lists every proposed intent with no approval as not reviewed, every non-rejected intent below the policy with how many approvals it still needs, every unanswered decision and every open thread. A proposal records the policy it was reviewed under, so a later change to the config never turns an approved proposal into an unapproved one or the reverse. Rejected intents never block.

useCases.name: Approve the reviewed intents
useCases.after: approve() refuses with every pending item while anything is pending; a proposal is approved when every intent is approved, amended or rejected and every decision and thread is resolved. Otherwise it returns an approved copy with status approved whose hash = sha256 over canonical JSON (keys sorted, undefined dropped) of the proposal without its hash, which binds the baseline: if the use cases changed since extraction, the approval is stale and the prose must be extracted again. Only an approved proposal can be derived, so only approved and amended intents generate proofs and reach whoever implements the change; they and the resulting use cases are the implementer's brief. An approved proposal cannot be reviewed; reopen() returns a copy without the hash, which must be approved again. isApproved() recomputes the hash, so any edit after approval is detected, and derive and apply reject a proposal that is not approved or was modified after approval.

useCases.name: Keep the review when the prose changes
useCases.after: Extracting a proposal's edited prose again carries the previous review over. A new intent with the same change, use case and description, ignoring case and whitespace, as a previously reviewed (non-proposed) intent takes its status, approvals, review note and original description. If instead the AI repeats the original reading of an amended intent for the same use case and quote, the amendment is reapplied with its approvals. Everything else stays proposed, so intents that changed lose their approvals. Decisions with the same question keep their answer when the option still exists, threads are kept, and the policy is kept. Decisions raised by the consistency check, and their intents, are not carried.

useCases.name: Derive the proof plan
useCases.after: derive(proposal) requires an approved proposal and asks the LLM (step "derive") with the models declared in .lastro/config.json, each touched use case's before and after with its approved and amended intents, the existing proofs of those use cases, each decision's question and answer (the chosen or else the recommended option) and notPromised. It writes pending proofs into the proposal, numbered P-n.PF-nn: each has a slug, name and description, the intent and use case it checks, the model and subject it runs against, and a check that is either a clause (requires and ensures in LSL, assumptions used) or a scenario (concrete input and an LSL expect); plus assumptions and beyondProof items. Every remove intent gets a proof, written from the use case's before, that the old behavior no longer happens; when the model cannot express it, derivation returns a decision for the reviewer and the proposal cannot be applied while it is open. Derivation never retires a proof: the proposal's supersedes is the union of replaces over the approved and amended intents, each new proof that takes the place of one lists it, and an existing proof the approved behavior breaks that no approved intent replaces comes back as a decision that sends the intent back to review with the proof added to its replaces. Every expression is parsed and validated. The proposal moves to proving. Without an LLM transport or a custom deriver, derive() throws.

useCases.name: Keep proofs as regression tests
useCases.after: A proof that passed belongs to its use case, stored in the use case's file with its id, the intent and proposal it came from, its model, subject and check. prove(proposal) runs the proposal's pending proofs and the proofs of every use case except the ones the proposal supersedes, so a change that breaks any use case fails as a regression, on a touched use case or not; a superseded proof that still passes is noted, since the behavior may not have changed; failures go back to the implementer through feedback. lastro regress runs every use case's proofs alone, for example in CI. A use case with no proofs yet is reported as unproved rather than failing.

useCases.name: Apply a proposal
useCases.after: apply(proposal), in the library and as lastro apply <proposal>, refuses unless the proposal is approved, unchanged since approval, has no open decision, and every proof, new and regression, passes. It then writes each resulting use case (adds the use case file, replaces the description and name, or deletes the file of a removed use case), moves each passing proof into its use case as a regression test, removes the superseded proofs, appends the proposal id to each touched use case's history, records the new baseline hash in the receipt and sets the proposal's status to applied.

useCases.name: Render a receipt
useCases.after: The receipt is Markdown for a pull request, written next to the proposal: the overall result and counts per verdict; the proposal and plan hashes; the Rust check with coverage, table digest and whether verdicts agree; the use-case diff, with each use case added, modified (before and after) or removed with the intents behind it, each replaced proof next to the proofs that take its place, each superseded proof that still passes, each regression and, after apply, the new baseline hash; a table of intents with verdict, evidence, confidence and what backs each; notes; each proof with verdict, evidence, method (exhaustive, samples with failure bound, traces), mutants killed, formal statement, counterexample, violating trace and notes; trusted pieces; where proof stops; not promised; and pending contradictions.

useCases.name: Run the pipeline from a CLI
useCases.after: The CLIs (lastro in TypeScript and .NET, lastro-go in Go) run init --model model.json [--approvals N], propose <prose-file> [--section <heading>] [--as <submitter>], status [<proposal>], review <proposal> --as <name> approve|approve-all|amend|reject|answer|comment|resolve, derive <proposal>, prove <proposal>, feedback <proposal>, apply <proposal> and regress. Each prints one JSON object and keeps state in a workspace directory (default .lastro, --dir to change): config.json (models, subjects and the review block), usecases/, proposals/ with each proposal's receipt, and llm/. init --approvals writes review.approvals. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 not ok (review pending, contradictions, failing proofs or regressions, apply refused), 2 usage or error, 3 an LLM answer is needed. derive refuses while review is pending and, on contradictions, writes the returned decisions into the proposal.

useCases.name: Share one workspace across CLIs
useCases.after: The TypeScript, .NET and Go CLIs read and write the same .lastro/ files (config.json, usecases/, proposals/ and llm/), so one can propose, another review, and a third derive, prove and apply. A proposal approved by one SDK has a valid approval hash for the others, and proofs and baselines hash the same in all three.

useCases.name: Gate an agent's code edits on reviewed intents
useCases.after: The Lastro plugin for Claude Code and Codex (plugins/lastro) is active in a repository that has .lastro/plugin.json. Its PreToolUse hook treats the first attempt to edit source code, in any mode (plan mode, auto mode, an informal plan or none), as the moment to extract intents: edit tools (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, apply_patch) on code outside .lastro/ and outside the configured allow globs are denied, with steps to write the change as prose in .lastro/proposals/<id>-<slug>.md, run lastro propose and start the user's review, unless the current proposal is approved, its proofs were derived from exactly its current intents and decisions, and its last proof run has not passed yet. Once every proof passes, the next source edit is a new change and is denied the same way. With gate "off" it never blocks. Proposals and handoff answers inside .lastro/ are always allowed; the proposal and use-case JSON files, receipts, config.json and the plugin's state are denied because only the CLI writes them; edits to .lastro/plugin.json ask the user in Claude Code and are denied in Codex. SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit add the progress board and the rule that the agent is the author of the proposal and never approves it.

useCases.name: Review an agent's proposal like a pull request
useCases.after: The plugin's propose skill has the agent write the change as prose in .lastro/proposals/<id>-<slug>.md, run lastro propose (answering handoffs itself), then ask the user every open decision and, per intent, shown with the existing proofs it replaces, approve, request changes (amend) or reject, recording only the user's answers with lastro review --as <user>, until lastro status is ready; then lastro derive writes the proposal's proofs. The PreToolUse hook makes every lastro review command that approves, answers, amends or rejects show a Claude Code permission prompt, and denies it in both harnesses when --as names an agent (claude, codex, agent, assistant, ai, bot). With a policy above one approval the board shows each intent's approvals out of the required number and the proposal waits for the other reviewers.

useCases.name: Prove the agent's implementation when it stops
useCases.after: With a derived proposal, the plugin's Stop hook runs the configured build command and lastro prove --stream with the configured arguments, appending the events to .lastro/plugin/progress.jsonl after a build event. Failing proofs or regressions in other use cases (or a failed build, recorded as a result event with its error) block the stop and return the failures and counterexamples to the agent as its next instruction, numbered against maxIterations (default 5) per proposal; after that the stop goes through and the user takes over. Passing proofs, or an unchanged code base whose last proof passed, end the turn. A code edit after a proof marks it stale in .lastro/plugin/state.json, so the next stop proves again.

useCases.name: Show the proposal's progress board
useCases.after: The plugin renders, from the CLI's status output and the files in .lastro/, a board for the current proposal with the stages (intents extracted, decisions answered, intents approved per the policy, proofs derived, verification), the existing proofs its intents replace, any regression in other use cases, and one line per proof: ✓ proved, ≈ evidenced, ✗ violated with its counterexample, ! weak or vacuous, ○ pending, plus the beyond-proof intents and the next step. It is shown to the user after every lastro command and on every stop, added to the agent's context on session start and on each prompt, and printed by lastro-plugin.mjs board (or one line with --line, for a status line); lastro-plugin.mjs prove builds, proves and prints it.

useCases.name: Show approvals and proofs live beside the chat
useCases.after: The lastro-board mod for Claude Code (plugins/lastro-board) reads .lastro/ once a second when the session starts in a repository with a Lastro workspace: config, the current proposal, the use cases and the plugin's progress.jsonl. It opens a pane with the review (each decision answered or not, each intent with its approvals out of the policy's count and the proofs it replaces) and the proofs (○ pending, … running, ✓ proved, ≈ evidenced, ✗ violated with its counterexample, ! weak or vacuous, and the beyond-proof intents), updating each proof as the run under way reports it. It shows a one-line summary above the prompt and in the status line, and a toast when every intent is approved and when a proof run ends. /lastro-board opens the pane. It decides nothing and works only in Claude Code.

useCases.name: Turn an agent's plan into a proposal
useCases.after: When Claude Code leaves plan mode (ExitPlanMode), the plugin's PostToolUse hook saves the approved plan as the prose of a new proposal, .lastro/proposals/<id>-<slug>.md with the next proposal id and the slug taken from its first heading, and tells the agent to rewrite it as behavior, run lastro propose on it and start the user's review before editing source. After Codex's update_plan it adds the same reminder. Plans made any other way are caught by the gate on the first source edit.

useCases.name: Use Lastro from TypeScript, .NET or Go
useCases.after: Three SDKs expose the same pipeline (propose against the use cases, review with threads, pending, derive, returnDecisions, prove with the regression run, apply, gap review) with the same entities (use case, proposal, intent, proof), wire format, canonical hashes, seeded sampling, verdicts, receipts and prompts. Cross-check tests compare the .NET and Go reports and hashes with the TypeScript SDK, and all three with the Rust prover, on the reference login and its planted bugs.

useCases.name: Explore the pipeline in the sandbox
useCases.after: A web app (Vite, React, shadcn/ui) runs the real TypeScript SDK and the WASM prover on a store-login example with its own use cases. Under the pipeline gates, a feedback banner says what Lastro needs next and from whom: the team when review is pending or the spec contradicts itself (with a button that sends the contradictions back as decisions), whoever writes the code when proofs fail or a regression appears (the agent brief with counterexamples, copyable, with the same count as the Prove gate), or that every gate passes. The prose panel shows the example as a proposal: the intent map and, in one tab, intents grouped by use case as changes (add, modify, remove) with a before and after diff and the proofs each replaces, intent cards (approve, amend, reject, comment) with each decision card under the first intent it affects that is not yet approved (or its first intent once all are), collapsed to its answer once settled, with reviewers Ana and Bruno and a one- or two-approval policy; edited prose is extracted again by Claude (the page's Claude on claude.ai, or a dev-server endpoint with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), the review is carried over, and new proofs are derived. The code panel edits the implementation, and plants bugs shown as a diff. The contrast panel shows per-proof verdicts from both engines, regressions in the other use cases, mutants, runnable counterexamples, LSL and SMT-LIB2, the intent roll-up, trusted pieces, where proof stops, a production-trace toggle, a single-login runner and the receipt.

decisions.name: Old workspaces
decisions.question: What happens to existing intents.json workspaces (intent-artifact/v0)?

options.label: Import as a proposal
options.consequence: lastro propose --import turns intents.json into an open proposal whose intents must be mapped to use cases in review.

options.label: Refuse and re-propose
options.consequence: Old workspaces are rejected with a message to run propose again.

decisions.name: Apply with unproved use cases
decisions.question: Can apply run while some use cases still have no proofs (the 38 existing ones)?

options.label: Yes, reported as unproved
options.consequence: Use cases with no proofs are reported as unproved and do not block apply; the receipt lists them.

options.label: No, prove them first
options.consequence: apply refuses until every use case has at least one proof.
